notes: Transcribed from the hand-written surfaces, not re-derived: serialize()/read() in Frame.h/Frame.cpp, the dataset row builders in ProjectEditorForms.cpp, the commit sub-appliers in ProjectEditorCommit.cpp, and applyDataset*Fields in ProjectHandlerEntities.cpp.
jsonKey names a Keys:: constant identifier; the literal spelling lives only in Frame.h.

Two declared defect fixes carry a 'defect' marker and describe the TARGET state, not today's behaviour: overviewDisplay is now serialized, and the read-side defaults for fftSamples/fftSamplingRate/ledHigh/index match the struct initializers.
value and numericValue are runtime values that today's serializer still writes into the document; they stay persist:always so project files round-trip byte-identically.

datasetWidgets.notes: Order is QMap key order (m_datasetWidgets), not insertion order. Installed dataset-scope widget extension packages (spec 0038) are appended after these rows, so a machine with no package installed sees exactly this domain and no stored index moves.

displayFormats.notes: The first six rows follow the legacy QMap key order (m_displayFormats); Hexadecimal and Binary append after them (spec 0108) so no stored index moves. The QMap is only an index-range guard.

valueFormats.notes: Dataset::format (spec 0108). An int domain is a parallelValues source: StaticMapOptions keys on strings.

plotOptions.notes: Order is QMap key order (m_plotOptions, keyed by QPair<plt,log>).

fftSampleCounts.notes: m_fftSamples; labels are the numbers themselves and are never translated. Not-found falls back to index 7 (1024).

fftWindows.notes: m_fftWindows / m_fftWindowValues; values are SerialStudio::FFTWindow. Not-found falls back to Blackman-Harris (5).

widgetExtensionOptions.notes: Appends the installed dataset-scope widget extension packages to the built-in widget domain (spec 0038 T20 residue); a package that replaces a built-in keeps the built-in row.

properties.label: Dataset Title
properties.description: The name shown on the dashboard and in exports.

wire.exclude: A computed dataset has no frame position and needs a transform, and code never rides the wire.

properties.label: Computed Dataset
properties.description: Calculates the value with a transform instead of reading it from the incoming data, so it needs no frame index.

properties.label: Hide on Dashboard
properties.description: Hides this dataset's own widget on the dashboard. Canvas widgets can still read its value.

properties.label: Frame Index
properties.description: Which value of each frame this dataset reads, counting from 1. Use 0 to leave it unassigned.
properties.apiError: Invalid index: must be >= 0 (0 = unassigned, 1+ = parser slot)
properties.defect: read-default was -1 while the struct initializes 0; the manifest default is the struct value

properties.label: Measurement Unit
properties.description: The unit shown next to the value, such as V or mA. Optional.

properties.label: Script Alias
properties.description: A short, unique name that scripts and the API can use to find this dataset. Optional.
properties.apiError: Alias '%1' is already used by another dataset; aliases must be unique across the project

properties.label: Widget Color
properties.description: The color of this dataset's plots and widgets. Automatic uses the theme's colors.
properties.apiError: Invalid color '%1': use '#rrggbb' or a valid color name; empty string restores the automatic theme color

properties.label: Minimum Value
properties.description: The lowest value this dataset is expected to reach. Widgets and the FFT plot use it when their own range is empty.

properties.label: Maximum Value
properties.description: The highest value this dataset is expected to reach. Widgets and the FFT plot use it when their own range is empty.

properties.label: Enable Plot Widget
properties.description: Plots the value over time.
properties.notes: One combo row drives both plt and log; the row's form id is kDatasetView_Plot.

properties.apiDescription: Include this dataset in CSV/data logging
properties.notes: No row of its own: edited through the Plt tuple row.

wire.exclude: Names another dataset's runtime unique id, which a device cannot know.

properties.label: X-Axis Source
properties.description: What the plot's horizontal axis shows: time, or another dataset.

properties.label: Logarithmic X Axis
properties.description: Uses a logarithmic scale for the horizontal axis. Available when the axis shows samples or a dataset, not time.

properties.label: Logarithmic Y Axis
properties.description: Uses a logarithmic scale for the vertical axis. Values at or below zero are drawn at the bottom.

properties.label: Enable FFT Analysis
properties.description: Shows how strong each frequency is in the signal.

properties.label: Enable Waterfall Plot
properties.description: Shows a scrolling picture of the signal's frequencies over time (Pro).

properties.label: Peak Ballistics
properties.description: Peaks jump up at once and fall back slowly over the release time, like a hardware audio analyzer.

properties.label: Ballistics Release (ms)
properties.description: How long a peak takes to fall back, from 50 to 5000 ms.

wire.exclude: Names another dataset's runtime unique id, which a device cannot know.

properties.label: Waterfall Y Axis
properties.description: What the waterfall's vertical axis shows: time (the default) or another dataset. Choosing an RPM dataset, for example, turns the waterfall into a Campbell diagram.

properties.label: FFT Window Size
properties.description: How many samples each frequency analysis uses. More samples show finer frequency detail but react more slowly.
properties.defect: read-default was -1 while the struct initializes 256; the manifest default is the struct value

properties.label: FFT Window Function
properties.description: Shapes each block of samples before the analysis so that nearby frequencies don't blur together. Used by the FFT plot and the waterfall.
properties.notes: Read side clamps an out-of-range value back to 5 (Blackman-Harris).

properties.label: FFT Sampling Rate (Hz, required)
properties.description: How many samples per second the device sends for this dataset. The frequency axis is only correct when this matches.
properties.defect: read-default was -1 while the struct initializes 100; the manifest default is the struct value

properties.label: Logarithmic Frequency Axis
properties.description: Uses a logarithmic frequency axis so low frequencies stay readable. Used by the FFT plot and the waterfall.

properties.label: Minimum Value (optional)
properties.description: The lowest value expected in the signal, used to scale the analysis. Leave empty to use the dataset's Minimum Value.

properties.label: Maximum Value (optional)
properties.description: The highest value expected in the signal, used to scale the analysis. Leave empty to use the dataset's Maximum Value.

properties.label: Widget
properties.description: The widget that shows this dataset on the dashboard.

properties.label: Tick Count
properties.description: How many major marks the dial shows. Use 0 to fit them to the widget's size.

properties.label: Label Format
properties.description: How numbers appear on gauge and bar marks and captions. Hexadecimal and Binary also apply wherever the value is shown as text.

properties.label: Decimal Points
properties.description: How many decimal places the value shows. Overrides Label Format. Use -1 for automatic.
properties.notes: The editor row is always editable and clamps at -1 only; the API additionally caps at 15.

properties.label: Minimum Value (optional)
properties.description: The lowest value on the gauge or bar. Leave empty to use the dataset's Minimum Value.

properties.label: Maximum Value (optional)
properties.description: The highest value on the gauge or bar. Leave empty to use the dataset's Maximum Value.

properties.label: Hold Min/Max Markers
properties.description: Marks the lowest and highest values seen since the data was last cleared.

properties.label: Suppress Alarms
properties.description: Keeps the alarm bands on the widget, but never sends notifications, raises alarms, or plays sounds for them.

properties.label: Alarms only while visible
properties.description: Sends notifications, raises alarms, and plays sounds for the bands only while a widget showing this dataset is on screen. Suppress Alarms still turns them off entirely.

properties.label: Alarm Deadband
properties.description: How far the value must move back out of a band, in the dataset's units, before that band can alarm again. Stops a value that hovers at a limit from alarming over and over. Use 0 for none.
properties.apiError: Invalid alarmDeadband: must be >= 0 (dataset units, 0 = no hysteresis)

properties.label: Show in LED Panel
properties.description: Shows this dataset as a light in the LED panel.

properties.label: LED On Threshold (required)
properties.description: The LED turns on when the value reaches this level. Use alarm bands for more than two states.
properties.defect: read-default was 0 while the struct initializes 80; the manifest default is the struct value

properties.apiDescription: Show this dataset in the project overview panel
properties.defect: the key was read and API-settable but never serialized; the write is restored here
properties.notes: kDatasetView_Overview builds no row today. The enumerator is kept so the form-id numbering is unchanged; wiring a row or dropping the id is a separate pass.

wire.exclude: Code; a declaration never carries a transform (spec 0111 R10).

properties.apiDescription: Per-dataset transform script; runs on every parsed value
properties.notes: Edited through the transform script editor, not a form row; the commit switch still handles the id.

wire.exclude: Belongs to the transform code, which never rides the wire.

properties.apiDescription: Transform script language: -1 inherit, 0 JavaScript, 1 Lua, 3 Expression

properties.label: Format
properties.description: Decodes the raw number before any transform: as fixed point, as a group of bits, or with a scale and offset.
properties.apiError: Invalid format: must be 0 (none), 1 (fixed point), 2 (bit field) or 3 (scale)
properties.notes: Spec 0108. The decoder runs on the value that feeds the dataset: the parsed value of a channel dataset, the transform's result of a computed one.

properties.label: Integer Width (bits)
properties.description: How many bits the raw number has, from 1 to 64. Numbers wider than 53 bits lose precision.

properties.label: Signed
properties.description: Reads the raw number as signed (two's complement) at this width.

properties.label: Fraction Bits
properties.description: The raw number is divided by 2 to this power. For example, the Q15 format uses 15.
properties.apiError: Invalid formatFractionBits: must be 0 to formatWidth - 1

properties.label: Bit Offset
properties.description: Where the field starts, counted in bits from the lowest bit (0).
properties.apiError: Invalid bit field: formatBitOffset + formatBitWidth must not exceed formatWidth

properties.label: Bit Count
properties.description: How many bits the field has. Use 1 for a single on/off flag.
properties.apiError: Invalid bit field: formatBitOffset + formatBitWidth must not exceed formatWidth

properties.label: Scale
properties.description: The raw number is multiplied by this value, then the offset is added.

properties.label: Offset
properties.description: Added to the value after it is multiplied by the scale.

properties.apiDescription: Text shown for a value no label row matches; empty shows the number
properties.notes: Spec 0108; edited in the Labels dialog as the table's catch-all row, not a form row.

Collection of FrequencyMarker; validated by DataModel::read(FrequencyMarker&).

wire.exclude: Parameters of transform code, which never rides the wire.

subEntities.notes: Named scalar parameters (number | string | bool) the dataset transform reads as `params` (spec 0083); nested values are dropped by the reader.

Value-to-text table (spec 0108): a JSON array of {value, text} the two hooks own whole, through the hook-driven map shape. The reader drops a non-integer or duplicate key and an empty text and sorts by value; an empty table writes nothing.
